statement: Asserting or ruling on system state from a summary/handback instead of checking current live state produces stale-but-confident claims when something else changes concurrently. Two instances, same day, different actors: (1) cejel PR #287 merged CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md text stating this repository has no local Maeve lesson store -- true when drafted, false 3 minutes later when PR #286 (a real holding directory with harvest+age-bound drain) landed first via the auto-merge queue, unchecked before treating #287 as final. (2) The operator ruled Cejel should have no local lesson store by reasoning from the prior handback's dead-end description, without checking currently-open PRs -- #286 was already open with the actual fix. A correct-when-formed claim needs a live re-check immediately before being asserted as current, especially right after any auto-merge or async landing.

anchors.summary: Merged CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md wording stating cejel has no local Maeve lesson store, three minutes after PR #286 (already contradicting it) landed via the same auto-merge queue -- author didn't re-check before treating #287 as final.

Gave cejel a real, age-bounded local Maeve lesson holding directory with a harvest-and-drain design, open concurrently while the operator separately ruled (in a different channel) that cejel should have no local store, without checking open PRs first.
